name: Cardinal Health
desc:
Coordinator, Individualized Care | $18.10-$25.80/hr | Inbound/Outbound, No Sales Expectations
Company: Cardinal Health (Sonexus Access and Patient Support)
Industry: Healthcare / Specialty Pharmacy Patient Support
What Your Day Will Look Like:
 Picture yourself as the connection point helping patients actually get and stay on specialty medications their doctor prescribed. You'd answer inbound calls from patients and physician offices, sorting out what they need and trying to solve it in one call whenever possible. You'll also make outbound calls for follow-ups, confirmations, or to track down missing information, and you'll work closely with physician offices, pharmacies, and your own internal team to keep everything moving. A real part of the job is watching for anything that needs to be flagged as an Adverse Event and documenting it properly. This is detailed, conversation-heavy work where you're typing information into the system while you talk, so multitasking between listening and documenting is a daily skill here.
assessment: Expect an assessment involving a typing test
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements
Education Minimum: High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent work experience preferred.
Required Experience: Not required outright. 1+ years of experience in a fast-paced call center environment is preferred, not mandatory.
Preferred Experience: Certified Pharmacy Technician credential.
Required Skills:
Basic computer knowledge, Microsoft systems, and telephony
Strong communication and customer service skills
Ability to work independently and stay self-directed
Comfortable sitting for long periods in a cubicle-style remote setup
Ability to prioritize multiple concurrent tasks with a sense of urgency
Best Fit
 This role is ideal for:
Someone who genuinely enjoys helping people solve a problem in one call rather than passing them around
Someone comfortable typing detailed notes into a system while actively talking on the phone
Someone self-directed who can work independently with only general guidance on routine tasks
Someone looking for a stable, benefits-rich healthcare-adjacent role without needing a specialty pharmacy background going in
Not a Good Fit for:
Anyone who can't commit to hardwired internet, since WiFi, satellite, cellular, and dial-up connections are explicitly not accepted
Anyone uncomfortable with mandatory on-camera attendance during new hire training
Anyone who needs a fully flexible schedule, since shifts fall within a set Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM CST window with possible overtime
Top 10 Resume Keywords:
One-call resolution
Inbound and outbound call handling
Patient and provider communication
Detail-oriented documentation
Multi-team coordination
Fast-paced call center environment
Confidential information handling
Time management under deadline pressure
Customer service and support
Independent, self-directed work
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process:
 Application → Assessment → Phone screen → Final interview. Total time to hire averages 3 to 15 days.
4-5 interview questions for this role:
Tell us about your experience in a fast-paced call center or customer service environment.
How do you handle taking detailed notes while actively speaking with someone on the phone?
Walk us through how you'd resolve a patient's issue in one call whenever possible.
What does staying self-directed and independent look like for you in a remote role?
How comfortable are you sitting for extended periods in a dedicated home workspace?
other:
Pay, Shift, Benefits, Background, Drug Test Information, and Career Pathway:
Pay: $18.10 to $25.80/hr, anticipated range. Actual pay depends on geographic location, education, experience, skills, and internal pay equity. Not bonus eligible.
Shift: Full-time, 40 hours a week, flexible scheduling required within Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM CST. Overtime may be required at times. New hire training runs 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM CST with mandatory on-camera attendance.
Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, Health Savings Account (HSA), 401(k) savings plan, early wage access through myFlexPay, Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs), short and long-term disability coverage, work-life resources, paid parental leave, and healthy lifestyle programs.
Equipment Provided: Provided. Cardinal Health supplies the computer, technology, and equipment needed for the role. Participant is responsible for their own high-speed internet, specifically a secure, hardwired broadband connection (DSL, Cable, or Fiber) at minimum 15 Mbps download and 5 Mbps upload, with a maximum 30ms ping rate. WiFi, satellite, cellular, and dial-up connections are not accepted, and a surge protector with network line protection is required for company-issued equipment.
Felony Friendly?: Not stated. Worth noting the posting does encourage applications from back-to-work candidates, people with disabilities, those without a college degree, and Veterans.
Drug Test: Not stated.
Notes: This is a genuinely solid, entry-level-friendly healthcare role since no prior call center or pharmacy experience is strictly required, just preferred. The internet requirements are stricter than average (hardwired only, specific speed and latency thresholds), so confirm a participant's home setup honestly before they apply. Pay reflects internal pay equity rather than a flat rate, so it's worth setting realistic expectations rather than promising the top of the range. Application window is anticipated to close 11/15/2026, so encourage prompt applications.
Career Pathway: Not stated directly in posting. Reasonable inferred path: Coordinator, Individualized Care → Senior Patient Support Coordinator → Team Lead → Patient Access Program Manager, though this is an estimate, not confirmed by Cardinal Health directly.
